OmaStats 1.6 shows which processes use each GPU and how much power the CPU draws, fills its process lists the moment you open it, and adds an inline bar label.

[Download the complete plugin](https://github.com/crmne/omastats/releases/download/v1.6.0/omastats-v1.6.0.tar.gz), or install it with:

```sh
omarchy plugin add https://github.com/crmne/omastats.git --enable
```

![The GPU page lists the processes using each card, and the CPU header shows package power, using synthetic demo data](https://github.com/crmne/omastats/releases/download/v1.6.0/omastats-1.6.0-gpu-cpu-dark.png)

## New

- **See which processes use each GPU.** Every card on the GPU page lists the processes using it, with how busy each keeps the card and how much memory it holds: VRAM on a discrete card, shared memory on an integrated one. AMD, Intel and other open drivers report this for your own processes without root; NVIDIA cards get it from `nvidia-smi`. By @crmne.
- **CPU power in the CPU header.** On an AMD processor with integrated graphics, the package power was shown as the Radeon card's power, and some Ryzen 7000 and 9000 drivers report it a thousand times too small, so it read 0 W. It now shows on the CPU, corrected. Intel and other AMD processors show it when their energy counters are readable, which takes a udev rule since the kernel keeps them root-only. By @crmne.
- **Inline bar labels.** A third choice under Settings, Bar labels, writes each readout's short name on one line ("CPU 23%") instead of stacking its letters. The default is unchanged. By @RobertoLipovan (#19).

![Stacked letters and the new inline labels, dark and light, using synthetic demo data](https://github.com/crmne/omastats/releases/download/v1.6.0/omastats-1.6.0-inline-labels.png)

## Fixed

- **Process lists show real figures when you open the panel.** A process's CPU share is the difference between two readings, and the first update after opening had only one, so every list said "Nothing busy" for a second. The lists now show "Measuring…" for a moment, then real figures. By @crmne.
- **The memory legend matches its rings.** Swap shared the Apps colour and its dot was always red, Compressed had a dot but no segment, and Total sat below figures that are not part of it. Swap now has its own colour that its dot follows, and the rows run in ring order with Total under the four that add up to it. By @crmne; thanks @ardentperf (#26).

![The memory breakdown before and after, dark and light, using synthetic demo data](https://github.com/crmne/omastats/releases/download/v1.6.0/omastats-1.6.0-memory-legend.png)

- **Text fields never read the clipboard, even while you type.** 1.5.1 kept the process search and the color fields from reading the clipboard until focused, but a focused field still read whatever another application offered. Both are now built from key presses alone, with nothing listening to the clipboard. By @crmne; thanks @HANCORE-linux (omacom/omarchy-plugin-marketplace#11213).
- **A shorter note under network processes.** It now says that only TCP is counted, so some browser and game traffic is missing. By @crmne.

## Known limitations

- The process search and color fields take typed text only: there is no paste or text selection.
- GPU process lists from open drivers show only your own processes. An integrated AMD card's own load figure jumps between 0% and 100%, so it can disagree with its process list.
- CPU power on Intel, and on AMD without integrated graphics, needs a udev rule that makes `/sys/class/powercap/*/energy_uj` readable.
- Version 1.4.1 and earlier can't read a disk saved by id. If you go back to an older version, choose the disk again in Settings.
- A mirror, raidz or striped ZFS pool counts against its first data drive only. "All disks" is correct, but picking another drive in the pool shows no space for it.
- A vertical bar with many readouts turned on can run into the bar's center section. Turn off readouts you don't need, or use figure-only looks.

## Thanks

Thanks @RobertoLipovan for the inline labels, @ardentperf for the detailed report on the memory legend, and @HANCORE-linux for following up on the clipboard during the marketplace review.
